transcript:
Meeting header: 2029-10-24 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Recorded by Fireflies
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (OmniRetail Head of Search), Daniel Park (Platform), Lena Cho (Security), Marcus Nguyen (Data Science)

Summary:
Customer evaluating options to serve embeddings + rerank for product search across 40M SKUs. Interested in hosted for POC, then Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for production. Main concerns: tail latency, cost at 500-1k QPS, vector DB integration (they use Redis Vector + occasional FAISS offline), embedding dimensionality (768 vs 1536), quantization/regression risks, SOC2/KMS. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing and run benchmark with a 10k sample.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality, hybrid search (keyword+embed), rerank architecture, hosting tradeoffs, security/KMS, benchmark plan, fallback & model variants.

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intro — I'm Alex AE on Redwood, and Priya is our SE.
[00:10] Sofia Martinez: hi all, Sofia here. We're trying to figure out how to scale our product search. We've got about ~40 million items, global region set, and right now we do a hybrid search with keyword then a light ML rerank.
[00:23] Priya Rao: cool, can you say what your current traffic looks like? QPS, p50/p95 latencies?
[00:28] Daniel Park: sure. Peak is around 750 QPS across regions; p50 search latency is 40ms, p95 is about 250ms — the p95 is the pain. We want tail under 150ms end-to-end for queries that include embedding lookup + rerank.
[00:40] Marcus Nguyen: we're running Redis vector for real-time lookup, but we also run batch FAISS indexes offline for cold queries. We're worried about fanout cost — top-k 100 from the vector DB then rerank top 10 is our current plan.
[00:54] Priya Rao: ok, so typical architecture we see is: embedding model (on Redwood hosted or customer's infra), vector DB fanout to fetch candidates, then a Redwood model (or model variant) for rerank — the tradeoffs are where you host the reranker and the embedding service.
[01:08] Lena Cho: and from security side we need SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for keys, and VPC peering for Private. Also data residency — EU region for our EU customers.
[01:20] Alex Chen: good, we support KMS and HSM integrations and have Private deployments with customer VPC and optional on-prem packaging. Our SOC2 docs are in the link we'll share.
[01:30] Sofia Martinez: perfect. Two main questions: 1) should we run Hosted for the POC and move to Dedicated later, or start Private now? 2) for embeddings, do we use 1536 dims for accuracy or 768 dims for cost/throughput — also what about quantization?
[01:45] Priya Rao: short answer: start Hosted for a quick POC, run the benchmark, then decide. For dims — 1536 will likely increase recall but at cost of slower throughput and larger index; quantization (int8 or Q4 variants) is useful but you need to validate accuracy on your eval set. We'll help run AB tests.
[02:03] Marcus Nguyen: our initial simulations show roughly 2x index size for 1536 vs 768, and latency at the vector DB lookup is also impacted (network transfer + decode). But rerank costs also grow if the candidate set is bigger — we use top-k 100 currently because for some queries we need the long tail.
[02:20] Daniel Park: about throughput, Redwood, can your hosted offering sustain 750 QPS with a reranker step at p95 < 150ms? We're concerned about continuous batching and tail bursts.
[02:31] Priya Rao: yes — hosted can. We have a couple of knobs: batching windows, continuous batching, KV prefix caching for repeated prefixes (some queries are very similar), and model variants for fast rerankers. For 750 QPS, we typically suggest Dedicated if you need predictable latency guarantees; Hosted can handle POC and bursty traffic but Dedicated gives autoscaling and reserved capacity to hit the SLOs.
[02:50] Sofia Martinez: and how does fanout to Redis affect cost? If we do top-k 100 at 750 QPS, we have a lot of vector ops.
[02:58] Alex Chen: right, that's a big driver. Options: 1) reduce fanout by doing a cheap lexical filter first (we do hybrid routing), 2) use a smaller candidate set then do a two-stage rerank, 3) use caching for popular queries. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and caching policies to reduce per-query token cost and vector DB ops.
[03:16] Marcus Nguyen: are there recommendations for quantizing embeddings? our embedding model exports float32 vectors currently. We want to compress to save memory but not lose search quality.
[03:24] Priya Rao: we typically recommend trying 8-bit/INT8 or product quantization first — a Q4_K_M style quant will keep good quality for many workloads. But you'll need to run recall/regression tests. Our eval hooks can run your 200 queries and return recall delta vs baseline.
[03:40] Daniel Park: what's the operational complexity for Private? We have strict VPC rules and limited internet egress for the cluster.
[03:46] Alex Chen: Private supports customer VPC peering and can be deployed with no egress if needed. We also offer an on-prem bundle for fully air-gapped installs, but that has a longer lead time and additional support contract. For KMS, we integrate with common providers and HSM if requested.
[04:00] Lena Cho: do you provide audit logs at the token/request level? We need traceability for compliance.
[04:05] Priya Rao: yes, we provide per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns in Redwood Console. For Private, you can send logs to your SIEM or we can keep copies depending on the hosting path.
[04:15] Sofia Martinez: ok, let's talk numbers — cost ballpark. If we do Hosted rerank for 1M queries, what order of magnitude are we looking at?
[04:23] Alex Chen: ballpark depends on model size and candidate set. For a small reranker model and 10 candidates you'd be lower, but with top-k 100 and reranking top 10, plus embedding lookups, you'd see higher vector DB egress + compute. We'll send a detailed cost model, but expect Hosted POC to be the lowest commitment; Dedicated gets lower per-query once you commit.
[04:40] Marcus Nguyen: a practical question on integration — can Redwood call our Redis Vector endpoints directly, or do we need to proxy through Redwood?
[04:47] Priya Rao: both patterns exist. For Hosted, you typically host the vector DB and Redwood will reach it over private peering or a secure endpoint; for Private, everything runs in your VPC so the calls are local. We can also recommend using an adapter to batch vector queries to reduce RPCs.
[05:02] Daniel Park: curious about fallback behavior — if dedicated pool is saturated can you automatically fall back to smaller models or hosted?
[05:09] Alex Chen: yes, smart routing supports fallback policies. You can configure a cost-first or latency-first fallback to compatible model variants or even a hosted pool for overflow. That keeps the app online during capacity events.
[05:20] Sofia Martinez: great. For our POC we want: hosted initial test in EU region, run 200-query eval with our 10k sample, measure recall changes for 768 vs 1536 dims and quantized configs, measure end-to-end p95 — can Redwood run that?
[05:32] Priya Rao: absolutely, we'll run the benchmark harness, run dims/quantization experiments, and give you a matrix of recall vs latency vs cost. We'll also include replication/sharding configs for your 40M index projection.
[05:45] Marcus Nguyen: what's the recommended candidate size for hybrid rerank? Some of our queries are long-tail — lowering top-k loses coverage.
[05:52] Priya Rao: for long-tail-heavy catalogs we recommend a dynamic candidate size: larger fanout for low-precision matches and smaller for strong lexical hits. Redwood Console supports per-route policies so you can tune that without code changes.
[06:06] Daniel Park: any gotchas for moving from Hosted to Dedicated? Downtime, data migration?
[06:12] Alex Chen: we do a rolling migration; usually no downtime — snapshots of your vector index and config are migrated; for private on-prem there is more work, and we do a runbook. We'll include migration guides in the docs.
[06:24] Lena Cho: we need a security questionnaire answered — typical enterprise form with encryption, key management, access controls, and penetration test results.
[06:31] Alex Chen: we'll push a completed security pack and the SOC2 link after this call.
[06:36] Sofia Martinez: ok sounds good. A few quick clarifying items: 1) Does Redwood host embedding model or do we host embeddings? 2) For rerank model variants, can we run our own model or must we use Redwood's?
[06:48] Priya Rao: you can do either. Many customers host the embedding generator close to their write path and use Redwood for rerank; others push embeddings to us and we serve both. For rerank you can bring your own model artifact (we have support for custom weights) or use our curated variants for predictable perf. We'll help with ops.
[07:05] Marcus Nguyen: one last question — how do you handle cache invalidation for embeddings when catalog updates happen frequently?
[07:11] Alex Chen: typical approach: TTL-based invalidation + event-driven invalidation. For hot items we recommend a write-through path where updates push new vectors to the vector DB and we invalidate prefix/KV caches. Redwood supports stream-based invalidation hooks.
[07:26] Priya Rao: ok, let's jot down next steps — we will: prepare pilot pricing + hosting scenarios, share security pack, assemble benchmark harness and run tests with your sample set, and schedule the performance workshop.
[07:38] Sofia Martinez: perfect. Anything else?
[07:40] Daniel Park: maybe just to confirm the POC timeline — we'd like results in two weeks.
[07:44] Priya Rao: we can do that if we get the sample vectors and queries by Monday.
[07:49] Sofia Martinez: we'll aim to upload by Oct 27.
[07:52] Alex Chen: great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the email and links.

Action items (in transcript):
- Alex to send pricing and security pack (SOC2 link)

End of call.
